estimates.measure_detail: Number of distinct categories in each participant’s retained idea list, including accepted/copied AI ideas. The predefined Specht and Buck system has 13 categories; a student assistant blind to condition categorized ideas. Unclassified and deleted ideas were excluded. sources.quote: Shapiro-Wilk: W=.874, p=.004; significant results suggest a deviation from normality

estimates.notes: The paper calls this a team outcome, but the score is calculated once per randomized human participant; the AI is not another participant or randomized cluster. Printed medians: human+AI mdn=5, human-only mdn=2. They are retained here because the specified stats object has no median fields; neither is entered as a mean. The text also prints mean=4.115 without identifying an arm, so both arm means remain null. The included AI-origin material comprises 115 accepted/copied suggestions, not all logged suggestions. The reported rB=.617 is kept as paper_effect.type=other to distinguish rank-biserial correlation from Pearson r or a standardized mean difference. The Shapiro-Wilk diagnostic for human-only scores is W=.874, p=.004; it is not the treatment-comparison test. Figure 3 is a boxplot; no quartiles, whiskers, outlier values, or other statistics were read off the graphic. No arm SDs, SEs, or confidence intervals are printed.

sources.quote: Shapiro-Wilk: human-only: W=.874, p=.004, human+AI: W=.902, p=.018)

estimates.notes: The mean=2.846 is printed without identifying an arm and is not assigned to either arm. The Mann-Whitney p value is printed as p=.830. No arm-specific means, SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or standardized effect are given for this contrast. Figure 4 contains boxplots without numeric labels for the summary values; its medians, quartiles, and whiskers were not transcribed. Normality diagnostics are human-only W=.874, p=.004 and human+AI W=.902, p=.018; these are separate from the between-arm U test. Excluding AI-origin ideas from the score does not make this an after_ai outcome: the human-authored ideas were generated during the assisted session.

This measures idea quantity within a participant’s explored categories. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 426), section 4.1, last paragraph before section 4.2.

estimates.notes: Printed medians: human+AI mdn=1 and human-only mdn=2. These are retained in notes, not substituted for arm means. Higher values indicate more ideas per explored category; this is fluency, not diversity across people. The Shapiro-Wilk checks are human-only W=.771, p<.001 and human+AI W=.831, p<.001; they are diagnostics rather than treatment tests. No arm means, SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or standardized effect are printed for this contrast.

estimates.notes: Table 2 prints human-origin totals of 87 for human+AI, 140 for human-only, and 227 across conditions. These are idea counts, not participant counts; n_units remains null because this outcome is analyzed per participant. The arm means are transcribed at the printed precision and are not recalculated from totals. The table also includes AI-origin suggestions and logged-corpus totals; only its human column supplies this estimate. No quantity-comparison test statistic, numerical p value, SD, SE, confidence interval, or standardized effect is printed. Section 4.1 says humans working alone contributed significantly more ideas, whereas section 5.1 says there was no significant difference in human idea counts. This internal inconsistency is unresolved; no inferential value is inferred from either statement.

not_extracted.what: S1-O5: Total logged idea quantity, including unaccepted AI suggestions; AI-origin suggestion quantity
not_extracted.reason: Table 2 includes logged AI suggestions that participants did not accept into their results. It therefore does not measure the output participants produced. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 424), section 3.1; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Table 2; PDF pp. 5–6 (printed pp. 425–426), section 4.1. The joint-quantity significance claim in section 5.1, PDF p. 7 (printed p. 427), does not specify whether it concerns accepted lists or the logged corpus and supplies no numerical contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1-O6: Pooled category coverage and category distribution by human versus AI origin
not_extracted.reason: This compares AI-origin suggestions against human-origin ideas pooled across both randomized arms. It is a descriptive comparison of idea sources, not a contrast between assigned assistance conditions or similarity across different participants’ outputs. PDF pp. 6–7 (printed pp. 426–427), section 4.2 and Figure 5. No percentages available only in the figure were transcribed.

not_extracted.what: S1-O7: Rate of introducing a new category after the brainstorming counterpart contributes
not_extracted.reason: This source/process comparison is restricted to the human+AI condition. It compares human and AI contributions within the same assisted sessions, not randomly assigned human assistance conditions. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 427), section 4.2.

not_extracted.what: Subjective perceptions of speed, breadth, inspiration, repetition, cognitive stimulation, cognitive inertia, and creativity
not_extracted.reason: These are participants’ open-ended self-reports, not scores on the output they produced. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 427), section 4.3.

not_extracted.what: Association between number of human-authored ideas and number of categories covered
not_extracted.reason: A correlation between two outcomes does not estimate the randomized assistance contrast. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 426), section 4.1: “We find a strong, significant, positive correlation (Spearman’s ρ=.817, p<.001)”.

not_extracted.what: Frequency of requests for AI suggestions
not_extracted.reason: This is tool-use activity within the assisted condition, not a score on creative output or an assigned-arm comparison. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), section 4: “Participants in the human+ai condition requested AI input 148 times (mean=5.7), but only a subset of these ideas is reflected in the final idea set.”.

open_items: Participant-level arm means for the flexibility and within-category fluency outcomes, and arm SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or suitable standardized mean effects for all extracted outcomes are not printed. The flexibility means without arm labels cannot fill either arm field; no values were inferred from the boxplots.
Total and per-arm randomized counts, the excluded participants’ assignments, and exclusion timing are not stated. Overall participation is reported, but cannot be assumed to be the randomized count.
The opposing significance statements for human-authored idea quantity in sections 4.1 and 5.1 remain unresolved; no numerical test of that contrast is printed.

The idea set and inferential statistics behind the joint-quantity claim in section 5.1 are not specified. It cannot be established that the claim concerns accepted participant results rather than the full logged corpus.
The prior under-review study whose data were reused is not bibliographically identified, leaving participant overlap with named publications unconfirmed.
The paper does not explicitly state the participant country or the release year of the named AI model.
notes: Read the complete markdown conversion and the complete PDF, including the reference list; checked both tables and all figures. No appendix, supplement, or public data repository is identified. The paper describes a course-based experiment with individual random assignment; it gives no evidence that each session was assigned a single arm. The setting is a Western European university, with students mostly enrolled in informatics; an explicit participant country is absent. Participant exclusions, PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), section 4: “Our study had 54 participants. We had to exclude the data of two students (due to incomplete data and due to a misunderstanding with regard to the task).”. No degrees of freedom, output counts, or AI contributions were used to infer participant counts. All extracted outcomes concern the assisted brainstorming session; none measures across-person diversity or unassisted performance after AI removal. The two flexibility hypotheses are central to the paper, but no preregistration or preregistered primary outcome is stated. The introduction refers to novelty and value analyses in the earlier under-review study, but reports no contrasts for those outcomes here. Medians, means without arm labels, and normality diagnostics are preserved in estimate notes with PDF quotations, without relabeling them as treatment means or treatment tests. Sources with empty fields lists support these notes or measurement definitions; each recorded numeric estimate field has exactly one mapped source. No effect sizes, mean differences, SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, or p values were calculated.
